claims.claim: Two concurrent publishers of the same named cache key via tempfile.mkstemp + os.fsync + os.replace (the production atomic primitive from platform/plugin/fsops.py) never expose a partial entry: across 1,000 cross-process interleavings with a paced reader classifying every observation, zero reads were PARTIAL and every trial ended in a well-defined winner (A or B, complete payload).

Mutation control: with the atomic replace removed (in-place overwrite carrying a torn-write window), the same reader observes hundreds of PARTIAL entries - the detector fires on the broken state and is silent on the atomic state, so the property test measures something.
After concurrent atomic publishes join, the cache parent contains no leftover .tmp-TST0174-* files (publisher removes its temp on every path, replace exhaust raises instead of leaking).

negative_controls.description: Atomic os.replace: zero partial reads across 1,000 dual-writer trials. In-place overwrite with a torn-write window: the same reader must observe at least one truncated or checksum-invalid entry (242 observed).

implementation.publish: tempfile.mkstemp + os.fsync + os.replace with PermissionError backoff
implementation.entry_layout: MAGIC T174\0 + uint32be length + sha256(payload) + payload (reader verifies checksum before classifying)
implementation.reader: CreateFileW with FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE|DELETE so a concurrent os.replace is never blocked by an observation (measured: without delete-sharing the trial loop storm-degrades ~1000x)
implementation.concurrency: two persistent writer PROCESSES (A, B) driven by atomically-written go files; coordinator reader classifies during each trial

observations.name: partial reads across 1,000 dual-writer atomic interleavings
observations.method: paced reader classifying every observation during concurrent tmp+os.replace

observations.name: winners across 1,000 trials
observations.measured: A=495 B=505 OLD=0 UNKNOWN=0 (every trial a complete new payload)
observations.method: post-join classify of the live entry

observations.method: same reader against in-place overwrite with a torn-write window (atomic replace removed)

observations.method: directory scan of the cache parent after writers join

residual_unknowns.claim: Production Cache.put (platform/plugin/cache.py) is content-addressed via hash_bytes, so two distinct payloads cannot share a key and the A-vs-B winner race cannot exist there; the named-key concurrent publish under test is measured on the probe-local publisher using the same atomic primitive (tmp + os.replace).
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: If a name-keyed production cache appears, re-bind the same two probes to its put path and keep publish_inplace as the detector control.
